extracted.intended_audience: Participating Clubs, Team Delegations, Club Affiliates, Media Partners, LOCs and other commercial/operational stakeholders involved in the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025™
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing ownership, use and exploitation of Media Rights, Marketing Rights, Competition Marks, ambush marketing prohibitions, approvals and operational restrictions for Participating Clubs and their affiliates during the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025™.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Any and all Media Rights, Marketing Rights, Intellectual Property Rights (including in relation to the Competition Marks) and all other commercial or other rights and opportunities in relation to the Competition shall be exclusively and solely owned and controlled, on a worldwide basis, by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as explicitly otherwise set forth, no Participating Club is entitled to directly or indirectly exploit or use any such rights; clubs are prohibited from challenging FIFA’s ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation and compliance by Participating Clubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must strictly comply with the Media and Marketing Regulations, notify Team Delegation Members, Club Affiliates and contracted third parties of the Regulations, and is fully responsible for compliance by those parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must inform Club Affiliates they have no Marketing or Media Rights related to the Competition; assist FIFA in resolving IP infringements or Ambush Marketing; indemnify and hold FIFA, LOC and related persons harmless against liabilities arising from non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No right of association
rubrics_metrics.description: No third party may, other than as permitted under these Media and Marketing Regulations or as separately authorised by FIFA, do anything which gives rise to any association between such third party and the Competition and/or FIFA, or which directly or indirectly exploits the goodwill associated with the Competition and/or FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a broad prohibition on creating implied sponsorship/association without FIFA authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification obligation for infringements
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs shall immediately notify FIFA, in writing, of any infringement of these Media and Marketing Regulations of which they become aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt written reporting is required to allow FIFA to act on infringements or ambush marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/assignment of conflicting local rights
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent local or national laws result in any rights in relation to the Competition being owned or controlled by any Confederation, Host or Participating Club, the relevant entity unconditionally assigns/transfers such rights to FIFA, free of any charge, in perpetuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon FIFA request the relevant parties must execute documents at their own cost to effect the assignment/waiver to enable FIFA’s exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club Marks — licence to FIFA and scope of FIFA usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club licenses to FIFA the right to use and/or sublicense the right to use, in perpetuity and free of charge, any Club Marks and the visual representations of Playing Equipment/uniforms in connection with the Club’s participation in the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA’s use/sublicense is exclusive for filming, recording and broadcasting of any Competition Match and non-exclusive for other uses (promotion, merchandise, games, etc.) FIFA may not apply variations to Club Marks or use them in ways that imply endorsement, are deceptive/misleading, damage reputation, sexualise/objectify/discriminate, or jeopardise club proprietary interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on FIFA use of Club Marks (format & prominence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for mere editorial uses, FIFA shall not use a Club Mark on a stand-alone basis and must always use any Club Mark with either a minimum of three other Club Marks or a Competition Mark; no single Club Mark used with others shall receive prominence over any other on a single item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial Partner usage of any Club Mark is also only permitted with a minimum of three other Club Marks. FIFA must not alter official versions of Club Marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team Delegation cooperation and image consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall ensure Team Delegation Members participate in a FIFA photo/video shoot and secure written confirmation from each Team Delegation Member of FIFA’s right to use (and sublicense) their records, names, photographs and images in perpetuity and free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA may not use images in a manner implying endorsement of commercial entities; FIFA’s rights are exclusive for filming/broadcasting matches and non-exclusive for other promotional/editorial/merchandising uses, subject to the no-endorsement restriction. Clubs must secure authorisations for player information (stats, history) use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of Competition Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA is and remains the sole owner of all Competition Marks, retaining the exclusive right to develop any marks, logos and symbols for the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This confirms FIFA ownership and control of competition branding, including official names, emblems, mascot, slogan, look, trophy and related elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on development/use of competing marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs, Club Affiliates and contracted third parties must not develop, use, register, adopt or create any mark, logo or symbol which refers to the Competition or which, in FIFA’s reasonable opinion, is confusingly similar to, a colourable imitation of, a derivation of, or which unfairly competes with any of the Competition Marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically refrains from use of terms such as 'Intercontinental Cup', 'Copa', 'Cup', 'FIFA', and similar translations; also prohibits using dates with host cities and other indicia that infer identification with FIFA or the Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No challenge to Competition Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs shall not oppose, nor ensure their Club Affiliates or contracted third parties oppose, FIFA trademark or copyright applications, nor seek to cancel any such registrations, or apply for protection that would adversely affect FIFA’s proprietary interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: does not apply where a Competition Mark includes an IP right belonging to a Participating Club (or affiliate/third party) that was registered prior to publication of these Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambush Marketing prohibition (anti-infringement undertaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clubs must ensure Club Affiliates and contracted third parties do not engage in or permit any Ambush Marketing activity that seeks unauthorised commercial association with the Competition or exploits its goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA emphasises ambush marketing can substantially diminish commercial value and financing of the Competition; clubs must actively prevent such activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to clubs of alleged violations (ambush/IP)
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA will notify a Participating Club if any of its Club Affiliates or contracted third parties is conducting activity which, in FIFA’s reasonable opinion, constitutes a violation of the Regulations, including IP infringement, unauthorised promotions involving Competition tickets/training access, restrictions on affiliate activities, or other ambush marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples enumerated: IP infringement, unauthorised competitions or promotions using tickets/access, infringing affiliate activities, and other ambush marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the ambush marketing provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambush marketing provisions apply even if the infringing activities are not directly connected to the relevant Club Affiliate’s or contracted third party’s association with the Participating Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA’s reach extends to otherwise unrelated commercial activities by affiliates that create association with the Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessation and remedies for ambush marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Following FIFA’s written notification of ambush marketing or further violation by any Club Affiliate or contracted third party, each Participating Club must ensure that the relevant entity immediately ceases and desists and provides FIFA written undertakings to refrain from further such activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must take all measures required by FIFA to secure cessation and undertakings; failure may lead to disciplinary action (see disciplinary clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use — editorial-only restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs are permitted to refer to the Competition only using the Competition Name and such use must be in an editorial context only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition Name usage is restricted to descriptive/editorial purposes; commercial/promotional uses are prohibited unless explicitly authorised by FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Logo creation and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs may create a Composite Logo incorporating the Official Emblem(s) and the Participating Club’s own emblem; the Composite Logo may only feature those emblems and the descriptive designation 'Finalist' and requires FIFA’s prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials to form a Composite Logo are downloadable from FIFAdigitalarchive.com; no other mark may be included without FIFA permission; all uses of Composite Logos must be submitted to ma.approvals@fifa.org for approval prior to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proximity and affiliation restrictions for Competition Marks and Composite Logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition Marks and Composite Logos may not be used in proximity to the names, logos or trademarks of Club Affiliates or any third party other than the Commercial Partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents implied association between affiliates/third parties and the Competition; exceptions only for appointed Commercial Partners or specific permitted designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses of Competition Marks and Composite Logo
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs may not use Competition Marks or Composite Logos: as part of advertising/promotional activity used with any Club Affiliate; on gifts, premiums, merchandise or clothing for sale to the public; or on official printed matter that also displays Club Affiliate names/logos (except where those parties are Competition Commercial Partners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such use is commercial and prohibited; editorial use inside publications is permitted under conditions (see printed materials rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Club-printed materials — cover and advertising restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed materials produced by Participating Clubs related to the Competition (posters, guides, programmes, magazines, maps, booklets, electronic publishing, etc.) must not feature Competition Marks or Composite Logos other than in a purely editorial context; if a Competition Mark or Composite Logo appears on front or back cover, no commercial identifications/advertisements shall appear on those covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition Marks may appear inside publications editorially, provided they do not appear on or opposite pages displaying commercial ads. Covers/titles must make clear publications are club, not FIFA/LOC, publications (example title provided). All such printed materials must be submitted for FIFA approval in advance (see approvals).

rubrics_metrics.name: No association between Club Affiliates and the Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs must ensure that no association whatsoever is created between their Club Affiliates (and contracted third parties) and the Competition in any of their promotional materials; Club Affiliates may not use Competition Marks or Composite Logos unless they are Commercial Partners or use a permitted designation like '[Sponsor] of [Participating Club] at the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025™'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict separation required to avoid implied sponsorship or affiliation; clubs must police affiliate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other marks and trophy identification prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs shall not use (and must ensure their Club Affiliates and contracted third parties do not use) any other marks, devices, symbols, logos or phrases to identify the Competition (including the Original Trophies and/or the Winner’s Trophies and/or any replicas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents creation of alternate branding evoking competition/trophy identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premiums (winner commemoratives) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Participating Club which wins the Competition may produce premiums commemorating their win only if: such premiums may include Team Identifiers but no other third party branding; may refer to the victory but shall not use Competition Marks or FIFA-owned IP without prior written FIFA approval; and may only be distributed free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners cannot commercially exploit Competition Marks or third-party branding on commemorative items without FIFA approval; distribution must be free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approvals process for use of Competition Marks and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposed uses of Competition Marks and Composite Logos, with summary of context and distribution channel, must be submitted to FIFA via the Marks Submission Forms on the FIFA Digital Archive platform or via ma.approvals@fifa.org; a sample of printed materials must also be submitted for prior written approval at least 30 days prior to the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission links to the competent FIFA approval coordinator; clubs must make requested changes to achieve compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club website requirements — link to FIFA.com and emblem use
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must include a link to the relevant language section of FIFA.com on every page of its website that features Competition-related content; this link shall comprise the Official Emblem(s) of the Competition which may not be used in any other manner or appear near Club Affiliate branding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official Emblem(s) are tightly controlled and may not be used elsewhere or near affiliate/third-party branding on club websites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club website syndication package
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs may obtain from the FIFA Partnerships & Media Division a FIFA.com content syndication package (including latest scores and headlines) to use with their websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syndication is an authorised way to display official Competition content on club sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online use of Competition Marks and Composite Logo on websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition Marks and Composite Logos may be used on Participating Club websites only for editorial purposes, only with FIFA’s prior written approval, not in association or proximity to commercial organisation names/logos (including Club Affiliates), not as hyperlinks, not in title/menu/footer bars, and always in compliance with article 13.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a link to another site is desired, a text link must be used instead of logo hyperlinking; prior approval is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: URLs restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Competition Name may not be placed in the URLs of Participating Club websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents using the Competition Name as part of web addresses which could imply affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition ticketing conditions and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must fully comply with all Competition ticket terms, conditions and regulations and ensure Club Guests comply; Clubs must refrain from any advertising/promotional activity involving Competition tickets or access (including sweepstakes, promotions, lotteries) that could be understood to involve FIFA or create association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must ensure Club Guests, Affiliates and contracted third parties follow ticket rules and refrain from promotional uses that could be seen as ambush marketing or imply transfer of tickets for promotional advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles — internal dissemination and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall be responsible for ensuring all Team Delegation Members have read and understood the Media and Marketing Regulations and shall immediately notify Club Affiliates and contracted third parties of the Regulations and require their compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs remain fully responsible for compliance by their team members, affiliates and contractors and for following further FIFA guidelines/directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Any violations of these Media and Marketing Regulations or other FIFA regulations that do not fall under another jurisdiction shall be dealt with by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee in accordance with the FIFA Disciplinary Code and relevant circulars and directives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance can lead to disciplinary sanctions under FIFA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited items and enforcement in Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Any items used in a Controlled Area by Participating Clubs or their Team Delegation Members which do not comply with these Regulations will be removed, confiscated, or covered up at the discretion of appropriate FIFA Officials; Participating Clubs may also face sanctions by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controlled Areas include stadiums, training sites, team hotels, media centres, accreditation centres and other places where accreditation is required; clubs must ensure items (kit, apparel, signage) comply with the Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No liability for FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA shall not be liable to a Participating Club for any losses, fees, damages or costs arising as a result of or in connection with the requirements contained in these Media and Marketing Regulations and/or the Competition or Equipment Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs accept responsibility for compliance costs and related losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of terms and drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalised terms have meanings set out in the Definitions section; words importing singular include plural and vice versa; expressions like 'including', 'in particular', 'for example' shall not limit the sense of the preceding words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Definitions to interpret obligations; beware that examples are non-exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedence / inconsistency clause
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent the Competition Regulations and Equipment Regulations are inconsistent with any aspect of these Media and Marketing Regulations, these Media and Marketing Regulations shall take precedence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant terms of Competition/Equipment Regulations shall be deemed amended accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and further guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA may amend these Media and Marketing Regulations at any time, at its sole discretion, upon notification to Participating Clubs, and may publish guidelines and circulars to elaborate or clarify aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must monitor for updates and follow any further FIFA-issued guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters not provided for — FIFA Council final determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any matters not expressly addressed in these Regulations (including force majeure) shall be determined by the FIFA Council, whose decision shall be binding and final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA Council rulings close gaps or resolve exceptional cases; clubs must accept finality of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages and authoritative text
rubrics_metrics.description: These Regulations exist in English, French and Spanish; in case of discrepancy the English text is authoritative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting obligations consult the English version where differences arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: No waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Any waiver by FIFA of any breach will not operate as a waiver of any other breach and is only valid if given in writing; FIFA’s failure to insist on strict adherence on one or more occasions is not a waiver of rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written waivers only; clubs should not rely on inconsistent past enforcement as future precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future editions non-precedential
rubrics_metrics.description: These Media and Marketing Regulations apply only to the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025™ and shall not apply to future editions; nothing may be relied upon as precedent for other FIFA competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules limited to this Competition; future competitions may have different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of Controlled Areas (applicability of rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlled Areas are defined to include Competition Stadiums (inside outer security perimeter), Official Training Sites, Team Hotels and FIFA hotels, locations of Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities, official ancillary events (banquet), International Broadcasting Centre(s), accreditation centres and any location requiring official Competition accreditation (stands, mixed zones, interview rooms, media and TV centres, VIP rooms, official FIFA/LOC functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much of the Media and Marketing Regulations (access, use of marks, equipment, media activities) apply specifically within these Controlled Areas and to individuals operating within them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of Media Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Rights mean the right to report upon, record, transmit or otherwise exploit still/moving images, audio-only material, audiovisual material, text and data by any means of any aspect of the Competition within any site on a live or delayed basis in any media, including rights to basic audiovisual feed, additional feeds, unilateral coverage, archive materials, commentary, official film and related products; includes Fixed Media Rights, Public Exhibition Rights, In-Flight Rights, In-Ship Rights and news access rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This comprehensive definition clarifies what FIFA controls and what clubs/affiliates may not exploit without FIFA rights/authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of Marketing Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing Rights mean in any and all media any and all advertising rights, promotional rights, rights of endorsement, rights of association, premium and giveaway rights, merchandising and licensing rights, concession rights, sponsorship rights, hospitality rights, travel and tourism rights, ticketing rights, accommodation rights, publishing rights, betting/gaming rights, retail rights, music rights and any other rights and/or associated commercial opportunities relating to the Competition to the extent such rights are not Media Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delineation shows marketing vs media rights; clubs must assume FIFA control over broad commercial categories unless expressly stated otherwise.
